classification: Documented SRDE benchmark extension and robustness test; established Bayesian observer learning and selection-bias methods, no first-ever claim
deployment: Three-step LA1 action graph, max two fresh reports and one lineage audit. Same terminal decisions and action costs for recursive/conventional methods. KnownAuditQ is an information-advantaged diagnostic, not budget-fair learned baseline.
information: Learners receive sanitized observation packets only. Later finer evidence replaces marginal evidence; baseline counts on selected references intentionally ignores missingness mechanism.
limits: Synthetic; fixed fitted q, no deployment retraining or drift. H is counterfactual calibration amortization, not an extra sampled test set. No independent empirical dataset in this study. Binary event truth and lineage are distinct; affect F is outside this experiment and never used as truth.
loss: Abstention=.15; otherwise squared probability error; plus deployment query costs and calibration total divided by H; Brier includes forecasts even if abstaining
primary: MixedSelectedBayes minus SelectedVerifiedCounts total expected per-case loss at H=512; paired stratified calibration-world bootstrap 1000 draws seed61621; fixed condition mixture
prior: discrete uniform q in {0,.01,...,1}; posterior mean quantized to nearest .01 with +1e-12 before Python round
question: Does one-factor typed delayed feedback improve audit-reliability estimation and downstream cost relative to selective verified counts, and does it repay calibration cost?
secondary: random-verified counts, FreshOnly, overlapping-factor negative control; specified vs source-model-error families; amortization horizons64/4096; q absolute error and interval coverage
verification: Perfect simulated lineage reference, requested only after Y arrives; random probability .25; selected probability .8 if audit agrees with model MAP L else .1; both capped32
